section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the above, the explanation of the Yom Kippur service in the Holy of Holies, which is the aspect of "one" in time, place, and soul, is understood, and from this service the Sukkah's covering is drawn.
section.t: And based on the above, the explanation and point of all the aforementioned matters will be understood.
And the concept is,
that the service of Yom Kippur in the Holy of Holies is in the time called in the verse35
"once a year."
And just as in time it is the aspect of "one" in time,
so too is it in the soul and in the world
(in place)
that it is in the aspect of "one" in soul and in place.
That the service is performed by the Kohen Gadol, who is the most holy and the aspect of "one" of the Jewish people,
and as it is stated36
"And he separated Aharon to sanctify him as holy of holies,"
and the service is in the Holy of Holies,
the place most holy of the entire world,
even from the place of the Sanctuary in the Holy Temple
(the Heichal).
And behold, upon the three aspects of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah (ABY"A) is founded the entire order of Hishtalshelut (the chain of descent), as it is drawn from its root and source
[and therefore Sefer Yetzirah is founded upon these three aspects],
until the creation is from His very Essence, blessed be He.
And as it is brought in Iggeret HaKodesh37

that the essence and selfhood of the Emanator, blessed be He, whose existence is from His own self and is not caused by any cause that preceded Him, G-d forbid, etc., He alone, with His power and ability, can create something from nothing and absolute non-existence.
And this is the matter of the aspect of "once a year,"
in the world
(place),
and in the soul,
that they become unified together in the service of the Kohen Gadol on Yom Kippur in the Holy of Holies,
the aspect of His Essence, blessed be He, which is drawn into the aspect of ABY"A.
And the aspect of "one" is drawn in revelation afterwards on Sukkot.
For it is explained in the Mishnah38
in the order of the Yom Kippur service, that the Kohen Gadol would wait in the Holy of Holies until the house was filled with smoke,
and from this smoke
(which is from the service of the aspect of "one")
is drawn the covering (schach) of the Sukkah on the festival of Sukkot39.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The beginning of the drawing of the aspect of "one" is on Rosh Hashanah, continuing through Yom Kippur into the inner aspect, and then revealed on Sukkot, affecting even the seventy nations.
section.t: And behold,
the beginning of the drawing of the aspect of "one" is on Rosh Hashanah,
for then is the service of "Make Me king over you,"
that they draw the kingship from the aspect of essential exaltation,
meaning that just as it is in the essential aspect, it will be drawn in revelation until it becomes "Make Me king over you,"
and by drawing that He becomes King of Israel
("Make Me king over you")
it is then drawn that He reigns over the entire world in His glory.
And the manner of kingship is through will,
and not only that His kingship rules over all.
For rule can be also by compulsion without will,
but Israel, through their service that "His kingship they accepted upon themselves with will,"
draw [this] into the entire reality,
into the entire order of Hishtalshelut,
to be "Come, let us bow down and kneel, let us bend the knee before Hashem, our Maker."40
And afterwards, on the tenth of the seventh month, the drawing comes in the aspect of pnimiyut (inwardness).
And afterwards, on the festival of Sukkot, the drawing comes in revelation.
That the victory that was on Rosh Hashanah,
beginning from the victory that from the King of Israel it is drawn that "His kingship rules over all,"
and on a higher level,
also "His kingship they accepted upon themselves with will,"
behold, it is drawn in revelation until it is drawn in revelation also in the world and also among the seventy nations,
therefore on Sukkot they sacrifice seventy bulls corresponding to the seventy nations41.
And behold, this drawing is drawn in revelation
(in the four days between Yom Kippur and Sukkot)
first in Torah and its commandments through the study of the laws of Sukkah and through the study of the laws of taking the Four Species,
for through study of this, even though it is in exile,
and even if the fulfillment of all the details is not applicable,
behold, it is as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said42
"I consider it as if they are occupied [with it]."
And by first effecting the drawing in revelation in Torah,
and afterwards drawing this also into action through the fulfillment of the commandments
[except that this is still the aspect of the action within the commandments themselves],
behold, it is then drawn into actuality also in the entire world,
that the entire world sees how a Jew fulfills the commandment.
And it is drawn in such a manner,
that it is stated in the Midrash43
that if the nations of the world knew what the Holy Temple was worth to them, they would surround it with fortresses to guard it, etc.
And this effect of the Holy Temple upon the nations is on Sukkot in a revealed manner through the sacrifice of seventy bulls corresponding to the seventy nations,
as is explained at length in the Midrashim of our Rabbis, of blessed memory44.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The Sukkah relates to the aspect of "one," and the statement that all Israel are fit to sit in one Sukkah is explained through the root of Jewish souls in the Essence (Atzmus), which is beyond even the level of "He and His Name alone."
section.t: And behold,
according to the above, that the concept of the Sukkah relates to the aspect of "once a year,"
and in the world
(in place)
and in the soul,
it is also understood why regarding Sukkot
(specifically)
it is stated "All the native-born in Israel [shall dwell in Sukkot]" and about this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expounded45
"All of Israel are fit to sit in one Sukkah,"
for the drawing of the aspect of "one" in revelation is on the festival of Sukkot.
And the explanation of the matter will be understood by prefacing what is to be clarified in this
[and as this precise point is also explained in the maamarim of our Nesi'im2],
why this teaching that "all of Israel are fit to sit in one Sukkah" is specifically from "All the native-born in Israel,"
for from "In Sukkot you shall dwell" one could also learn this teaching of "you shall dwell, all of you together."
And the general explanation of this
(in the language of Kabbalah),
is that initially
[i.e., before the Tzimtzum]
the Ein Sof filled all of the void space and there was no place for the existence of worlds
[meaning there was no possibility or existence for worlds],
and afterwards He removed His great light to the sides, etc., and there was drawn
(the great circle and)
the line (Kav),
and the entire length of the order of Hishtalshelut,
as explained in Etz Chaim at its beginning and in Mavo She'arim at its beginning
(as brought in many places and explained in Chassidus).
And behold, this aspect
(that filled the void space, etc., before the Tzimtzum)
is already called by the name Ein Sof,
and there is even some connection to the existence of worlds,
except that since the Ein Sof filled all of the void space, therefore there was no possibility for the existence of worlds.
But even there, there is a void,
and there is also the possibility that needs to be negated, saying that it is impossible for worlds to exist.
And above this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said46
"Before the world was created, He and His Name alone existed."
However,
even in this level
(already)
there are details,
"He,"
"and His Name,"
"alone,"
and they also say that the novelty of this level is that it is in the manner of "He was,"
as explained in the preceding maamar47.
However, His essence and selfhood, blessed be He, is above even this,
to the extent that it is impossible to say of Him that He is in the aspect of Sovev (transcendent)
(to the worlds)
and even not in the aspect of a distant Makif (encompassing light) and the like.
For His essence and selfhood, blessed be He, is not within the category of any matters at all,
to the extent that He is in the aspect of "There is none besides Him,"
and higher than this,
"There is none."
For "There is none besides Him" can be said when there is a category of "besides Him,"
but above this is the matter of "There is none,"
as this precise point is explained elsewhere.
And since Israel are rooted in His Essence, blessed be He,
it is understood that they have a connection and it is possible for them to reach and effect [something] in His Essence, blessed be He,
even as it is above, in the aspect of "There is none," even from the aspect of "He and His Name alone."
And this is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said48
"In whom did He take counsel? In the souls of the righteous,"
that the concept of taking counsel can be said of the very highest levels,
and even in the aspect that is above the category of place.
For since above all matters are through will and not through compulsion, G-d forbid,
it is understood that even in this level the concept of taking counsel applies.
And from this it is understood that the concept of taking counsel is, as it were, even in His Essence, blessed be He.
And about this it is said "In whom did He take counsel? In the souls of the righteous,"
which refers to the souls of Israel,
and "Your people are all righteous,"49
who are rooted in His Essence, blessed be He, and therefore they also reach His Essence, blessed be He.
And the concept of taking counsel is also with souls that are seemingly of a low level,
as is understood from the parable of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory50
who compares this matter to a father and a small son,
and since he compares the Holy One, blessed be He, to a father,
as it were,
it is understood that great and small are equal before Him.
For all matters are utterly incomparable to His Essence, blessed be He,
rather, it is so that it arose in His will that the souls of Israel,
and "Your people are all righteous,"
should be rooted in the Essence (Atzmus) itself,
and therefore the souls of Israel are rooted in His Essence, blessed be He.
